label: Positive record truth, admitted observation fibers and authentic anchors
term: sound positive historical records and uniform authenticity
definition: RecordsSound allowed observe positive content means: each admitted i whose observation is a positive record makes content (observe i) i true. positive o marks that o asserts the selected historical claim; content o i is the supplied primitive truth condition of that claim in the history indexed by i. SafeInitial is that implication at i. PositiveFibersTrue requires the admitted inverse image of each positive observation o to lie wholly in the set where content o is true. PositiveUniform says authenticity has the same truth value within each inhabited positive observation fiber; it permits uniformly false fibers. PositiveWitnesses gives at least one authentic input in each inhabited positive fiber. AuthenticityEvidenceOnly uses existing EvidenceOnly on the admitted subtype and the full vector of observation-equality tests; with all observations counted positive it is equivalent to PositiveUniform. This is a universal truth guarantee, not a definition of fallible knowledge, warrant or historical probability.
note: The independent primitives are admitted input class, observation map, positive-assertion classification and content truth condition. The theorems constrain their relationship; they do not complete the historical meaning of content, identify actual authentic traces, or justify choosing an admissible class. An ordinary example would supply the actual event producing a dated trace as content, and the currently read trace as observe; this application is OPEN. In the Boolean controls content is explicitly only agreement between a retained past marker and a reported bit. A uniformly false positive fiber is a concrete distinction between classificatory uniformity and truth. Empty admissible classes and unobserved fibers pass vacuously; controls retain inhabited positive fibers. No fake past is made metaphysically admissible and no equal prior or skeptical conclusion follows.
